speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the timeline of your right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and falls to begin my assessment. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if they have been getting worse? Also, you mentioned forgetfulness and paranoia; when did those behaviors start compared to your physical symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Frontotemporal Dementia with Motor Neuron Disease (or FTD with parkinsonism). The combination of 6 months of cognitive decline (forgetfulness, agitation, paranoia) preceding or concurrent with acute motor symptoms (right leg weakness, falls) in a 44-year-old male strongly suggests a neurodegenerative process affecting both cortical and motor pathways, such as FTD-MND or CJD. I will now request imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI.
